First, a distinction

3 Different Worlds of Performance

How it happens

People choose BUSYness over High Performance Every Day

Unclarity of Purpose, Strategy and Competency required are the big source of BUSYness.

Overactivity follows: with no filter for what matters, people react to everything.

Spread thin: time, energy and resources are diluted across too many things at once.

Shallow results: a lot of motion, very little meaningful progress.

Frustration: leaders and teams feel exhausted and dissatisfied.

More BUSYness: to escape the discomfort, they reach for more activity. The cycle repeats.

Where it starts

So who creates it?

The way out

Reflect. Own. Assert. Run.

The book's ROAR model turns the mirror into a practice, and it starts with the leader.

    Step 4 · Your team

    Bring your whole company in

    One leader cannot do this alone. These four steps work together. Start where it suits you, and each one makes the next easier.

    1. Run an awareness session

      A two-hour KILL BUSYness session that puts the same language and the same mirror in front of your leaders, and gets everyone ready to read.

      Request a session

    2. Follow the 30-day reading and implementation plan

      A plan you can hand to the whole company: who reads what, when to meet, and what to decide.

      See the 30-day plan
      Week 1 · Leaders firstThe leadership team reads the Introductory Chapter. Each leader takes the BUSYness Index, and the team compares scores.
      Week 2 · Everyone readsEvery team member gets a copy and starts reading. Hold the awareness session this week.
      Week 3 · DiscussThe reading club meets. One chapter, and one real decision in your business that it touches.
      Week 4 · DecideLeaders choose their first commitments, take their pledges and set a 30-day review.

    3. Start a reading club

      Your company runs it, using our guidelines. One chapter at a time, tied to real decisions in your business.

      Ask for the reading club guidelines

    4. Order the book for your team

      Everyone needs their own copy. Bulk discounts for teams, leadership cohorts and whole organizations.

      10+50+100+See bulk pricing

    Each step feeds the next. Together they take a company from reading the book to living it.

    Then implement: the 12-phase plan

    The first four phases take under 90 days and clear the ground. The remaining eight take about a year and build the foundation.

    First 90 days
    1Educate everyone on NFR
    2Implement NFR for yourself and your leadership team
    3Project Whitespace: empty your calendar by 50%
    4The Sensing Journey: deep connection and learning
    The following 12 months or so
    5Articulate or reconnect with purpose
    6Study competitive strategy and build an extraordinary one
    7Train the leaders
    8Redesign the organization in sync with strategy
    9Redesign performance management in sync with strategy
    10Train and develop people at every level
    11Put systems in place
    12Prototype, prototype, prototype

    The BUSYness Diagnostic

    A BUSY and a high performance organization, side by side.

    How purpose fades on its way down

    BUSY organization

    CEO / Founder
    Purpose: clear and felt
    Senior management
    Purpose: partial. Targets get louder.
    Managers
    Purpose: faint. KPIs dominate.
    Frontline
    Purpose: gone. Just a job.

    High performance organization

    CEO / Founder
    Purpose: clear and modelled
    Senior management
    Purpose: lives in decisions
    Managers
    Purpose: explains every task
    Frontline
    Purpose: alive, fulfilling a mission

    A schematic of the book's Purpose Transmission Gap, not measured data. Gallup (2025) finds about 70% of a team's engagement tied to the immediate manager.

    Two cultures, side by side
    BUSY organization
    High performance organization
    Meetings end with more meetings.
    Meetings end with decisions and named owners.
    Leaders spend 60-70% of time chasing what was already agreed.
    Commitments are honoured without reminders.
    Strategy is reviewed quarterly and forgotten by Monday.
    Strategy lives in daily decisions, not in a document.
    People arrive to complete tasks and go home.
    People arrive to fulfil a purpose, not just a job.
    Standards are quietly lowered when it gets hard.
    Standards are held firm under pressure.
    Departments protect their silos and blame each other.
    Cross-functional collaboration is genuine, not performed.
    Development happens when there is time, which is never.
    Leaders develop their people deliberately and consistently.
